source.notes: Artist's model of an Apple II set-up: the computer with an 'apple ][' badge, a monitor on a stand and two Disk II drives (the drives date the set-up to 1978 or later; the serial label on the model reads A2S2, the II Plus designation, so it is a type, not a specimen). glTF zip downloaded by the user from Sketchfab on 2026-10-09, 20 meshes, 9 PBR materials with 4096 px textures, 109 MB unpacked. Release date and price from the English Wikipedia 'Apple II (original)' infobox (on sale June 1977, US$1,298 with 4 KB, discontinued May 1979); no dimensions in the infobox or on Wikidata (Q201652), so they are left null and the display size comes from the model.

object.medium: Personal computer: beige injection-moulded plastic case with integrated keyboard, printed circuit board with MOS 6502; monitor and floppy drives
object.description: The Apple II was Steve Wozniak's second machine and Apple's first product for the home: a complete computer in a plastic case with a keyboard, colour graphics on an ordinary television and expansion slots inside. Introduced in April 1977 and on sale from June at US$1,298, it made Apple a company and, with VisiCalc in 1979, made the personal computer a business tool. The set-up shown adds the Disk II floppy drives of 1978 and a monitor; this is an artist's model of the type, not a particular machine.
facts: Wozniak gave the Apple II colour and sound by driving the television signal directly from the 6502's timing, a trick that kept the chip count low.
The eight expansion slots inside the case were insisted on by Wozniak over Steve Jobs's wish for two; they let the Apple II take a floppy controller in 1978.
VisiCalc, the first spreadsheet, ran only on the Apple II for its first year and sold many of the machines to businesses.
